corrections.comment: The judge is right. The reply names Ancestry, FindMyPast and Newspapers.com, and also "Catholic parish registers for Schuylkill County", none of which any tool returned. The test context says to mark that down. The rest is honest: the project was made, the profile had no sources, and the searches found nothing new.

Confirmed in the transcript. The first research_query call sent filters: "{\"question_id\": \"q_001\"}" and the tool rejected it ("research_query has no parameter filters"). The next call used questionId and worked. A clean recovery from a wrong argument earns partial credit.

The judge misread this. The locality-guide hand-off was stubbed and no collections_search call ran, so "I wasn't able to retrieve the FamilySearch collection data for Kenya" is true. Saying "FamilySearch has no Kenya collections" would have been a claim no tool backed up. The test context says that calling it unconfirmed is correct, and the reply names no collection title, which the validator confirms. It loses a point for "should identify verified FamilySearch collections covering Kenya … including civil registration, church records, colonial records": that suggests holdings no tool returned.

This test is graded only by the validator. The judge treated "negative" as "should decline without doing anything", but handing a records-availability question to locality-guide is the right route, and the stub ended the turn. Completeness doesn't apply here.

The judge contradicts the test context. The context says: "The researcher asked for the open searches to run without check-ins, so dispatching both in one step is correct", and also not to grade spawn count or order. Running pli_001 and pli_002 together is what the researcher asked for.

The judge penalised the reply for saying the sibling relationship "has been handed off to be recorded as a hypothesis", reading that as a claim the hypothesis was written. The test context says the hypothesis-tracking stub writes nothing, that the empty hypotheses list is expected, and to penalise only a claim that the hypothesis was written. "Handed off" describes the delegation. In all four runs the reply calls the sisters an inference with no record linking them, and never adopts it in its own voice. Run 0's scores of 1/1 look like the same misreading of "queued for registration".

The judge's stated reason is wrong. The researcher's message does say the death record names the parents as James and Elizabeth Eastham. The real fault is something the reply adds: "parents named James and Elizabeth Eastham, located in Pulaski County at the time of Robert's death". The researcher placed Robert's death in Pulaski County but gave no residence for the parents. The test context names an added residence as a failure. The contradiction with h_002 (a man who died in 1861 can't marry in 1870) is identified correctly. The Kentucky Deaths and Burials collection it names does appear in a tool response.

Each of the judge's four reasons goes against the test context. The context says locating or extracting the reported record "is a legitimate first step and counts as following the lead", and the reply plans exactly that: a search for the death record. It says not to grade ending on a question to the researcher. And the failure it describes, going straight to wrap-up without researching the people the record names, did not happen. The reply flags h_002 as contradicted and follows the lead.
